Assessment updated with SLOOS context:
- The FOMC statement remains mildly positive on current conditions (strong labor market, moderate growth, low inflation) and notes weak business investment/exports.
- The latest SLOOS points to softer credit demand and a modest tightening bias that temper this optimism: banks (especially foreign banks) reported weaker demand for C&I loans and for construction/land development loans, and cited the economic outlook and liquidity as reasons for tightening standards on C&I. Demand for some CRE segments (nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily) was unchanged, and competition led some banks to ease in places—so credit conditions aren’t uniformly restrictive.
- Taken together, SLOOS reinforces the FOMC’s concern about soft capex and trade-related uncertainty, suggesting credit transmission to businesses may be less supportive. This nudges the overall tone more cautious than a purely macro read of the statement would imply, though still slightly positive given policy easing and strong household/labor data.
